baseline: Host Linux 6.8.0-124-generic, prebuilt LTP 20260529 binary /nix/store/hik6kb512ia3p14lc2vwzb292d4k306a-ltp-20260529/testcases/bin/dup02, exit 0, 2 passed / 0 failed. dup02 is two TST_EXP_FAIL2 assertions, each requiring the call to return -1 with errno EBADF: 'dup02.c:27: TPASS: dup(-1) : EBADF (9)' and 'dup02.c:27: TPASS: dup(1500) : EBADF (9)'. Per assertion the correct kernel returns: dup(-1) => -1/EBADF because a negative oldfd is never a valid descriptor; dup(1500) => -1/EBADF because oldfd is validated as an open descriptor before any new descriptor is allocated, so an unopened high fd yields EBADF and not EMFILE.
root_cause: No defect. Asterinas already satisfies both assertions, and the two error paths are distinct. dup(-1): sys_dup converts the raw fd with `old_fd.try_into()?` (kernel/src/syscall/dup.rs:16), and the only TryFrom<RawFileDesc> for FileDesc (kernel/src/fs/file/file_table.rs:86-95) rejects any value < 0 with EBADF 'negative FDs are not valid' before the file table is touched. dup(1500): the conversion succeeds, then FileTable::dup_ceil (file_table.rs:115-142) calls duplicate_entry first (file_table.rs:157-164), which does self.table.get(fd.into()) and maps None to EBADF 'the FD does not exist'. Because duplicate_entry runs before get_min_free_fd/put_at, oldfd validity is checked before allocation, so an unopened fd 1500 cannot be reported as EMFILE. Note sys_dup deliberately does not consult RLIMIT_NOFILE on oldfd (only do_dup3 does, dup.rs:63-71), which is what keeps the 1500 case EBADF rather than a limit error. The pool entry is stale: test/initramfs/src/conformance/ltp/testcases/all.txt line 160 is still '# dup02'.
invariant: dup() must validate that oldfd refers to an open file description before allocating a new descriptor, so an oldfd that is negative or simply not open fails with EBADF regardless of its numeric magnitude or of RLIMIT_NOFILE; descriptor-space exhaustion (EMFILE) is only reachable once oldfd has been accepted.
linux_reference: Not read from source: this container has no kernel tree, its man pages are stripped to a 'system has been minimized' notice, and man7.org, elixir.bootlin.com and the mirrors returned by search were all refused by this environment's network policy, so fs/file.c could not be opened. The reference behaviour was instead observed directly against real Linux 6.8.0-124-generic by running the suite's own prebuilt dup02 binary on the host, which is the same authority the assertions encode: both cases return EBADF. In Linux this ordering lives in the syscall-entry/file-descriptor-table layer (fs/file.c SYSCALL_DEFINE1(dup), which resolves oldfd via fget_raw before get_unused_fd_flags), i.e. above any filesystem, and Asterinas places it in the equivalent layer: syscall entry plus FileTable in kernel/src/fs/file/file_table.rs.
other_callers: Nobody is affected, since there is no defect to reach. The two guards are shared rather than local to dup: TryFrom<RawFileDesc> for FileDesc is the single conversion used at every syscall boundary that takes an fd, and FileTable::duplicate_entry is shared by dup_ceil (sys_dup, F_DUPFD) and dup_exact (sys_dup2, sys_dup3), so the same EBADF ordering already holds for those callers.
suggested_direction: No kernel change. The whole fix is the pool edit: uncomment line 160 of test/initramfs/src/conformance/ltp/testcases/all.txt so '# dup02' becomes 'dup02'. Verify with the default configuration (no CONFORMANCE_TEST_WORKDIR override) and an empty selector, since the entry comes from all.txt rather than a blocked/ list.
